title: Integral compact supports have the prescribed reductions
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$. Fix $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Integral coefficients on a scheme $T$ mean modules over $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-étale site, not over the discrete constant sheaf $R$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-dimension]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Suppose that every derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^L A_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$, in the intrinsic sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For the integral and finite-level compact-support functors defined in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], one has

$$
Rf_!K\in D^b_c(Y,R),\qquad
(Rf_!K)\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}K_n\quad(n\geq1).
$$

Every displayed reduction has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. The displayed isomorphisms are the canonical compact-support coefficient comparisons, compatible with successive reductions.

proof.text: Fix the compactification $c_0$ defining the integral functor and put $M_n=Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}K_n$. The definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] gives intrinsic bounded constructibility of each $K_n$. Apply [lem-coef-finite-compact-support-uniform-tor] at every level with the hypothesized interval $[a,b]$. It gives intrinsic bounded constructibility and Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$ for every $M_n$, using a dense refinement only for the bound.

Apply [lem-coef-compact-support-normalized-realization] to $K$ and the same $c_0$. It provides a normalized DVR tower with a coherent realization, whose transitions are exactly the quotient-induced compact-support transitions in the definition of $Rf_!K$. Its invertible reduction adjoints are the canonical tensor coefficient comparisons, including their quotient cocycles.

By [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], the derived limit $M$ of this tower is derived complete and its projection-adjoint counit maps $M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}B_{Y,n}\to M_n$ are coherent isomorphisms. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] this is the defining limit $Rf_!K$. Step 2 identifies the actual transition maps, so these counit maps are the specified compact-support comparisons. Their coherence is the required compatibility with successive reductions.

Steps 1 and 3 give constructible reductions of $Rf_!K$ with Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$. In [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], test against the degree-zero coefficient module $B_{Y,n}$ itself: the tensor-unit identification is $x\otimes u\mapsto ux$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, on a K-flat model. Thus every reduction has cohomology zero outside that same interval. Derived completeness and these uniformly bounded constructible reductions are exactly [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], proving $Rf_!K\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ and the asserted reduction Tor bounds.
